messages.content: You answer multi-hop factual questions by searching the web. Do not rely on memory alone: confirm names, dates, and figures in retrieved snippets before committing. Give one final answer covering every part of the question.
Which is taller when measured from base to summit: Mauna Kea or Mount Everest, and by roughly how much, using commonly cited figures?

messages.reasoning_content: Everest wins on elevation above sea level, but Mauna Kea measured from its underwater base is taller overall. Need both figures.

function.name: search
function.arguments: {"query":"Mauna Kea height base to summit total"}

messages.content:
1. Mauna Kea — Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauna_Kea
   Measured from its base on the ocean floor, Mauna Kea is about 10,210 m (33,500 ft) tall — the tallest mountain on Earth — though only 4,207 m of it is above sea level.

2. Is Mauna Kea taller than Everest? — USGS — https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/mauna-kea-taller-everest
   Mauna Kea is the tallest mountain from base to peak; Mount Everest has the highest altitude.

messages.reasoning_content: Commonly cited: Mauna Kea ~10,210 m base-to-summit vs Everest 8,849 m; the base-to-summit figure for Everest is much smaller, but the usual comparison uses its sea-level elevation.

messages.content:
1. Mount Everest — Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Everest
   Everest's elevation of 8,848.86 m (29,031.7 ft) was jointly announced by China and Nepal in 2020.

2. How tall is Mount Everest, really? — https://www.nationalgeographic.com/everest-height
   The 2020 survey settled on 8,848.86 metres above sea level.

message.content: Measured base-to-summit, Mauna Kea is taller: about 10,210 m from its ocean-floor base, versus Everest’s 8,849 m above sea level. Using those commonly cited figures, Mauna Kea is roughly 1,360 m "taller", even though Everest remains the highest point on Earth.
